title: Ramadan: the month of the Qur'an
hook: Jibril reviewed the Qur'an with the Prophet ﷺ every Ramadan (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sha'ban, the month of getting ready, and your line, prepare the ground.

Ask what Ramadan is, and the usual answer is: the month Muslims fast. No food or drink from dawn to sunset, for a whole month. That's true. But open the Qur'an to the verse that sets up the fast, and it introduces the month by something else first. Not hunger. Not the dates at sunset. A book. The fast is there, in the next breath. But the month's name tag, in the Qur'an's own words, is about reading.

Surah Al-Baqarah, verse one hundred eighty-five. Pickthall: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind". The verse goes on to say the Qur'an is clear proofs of guidance and the criterion, the furqan from eleven days ago. Only then does it say: whoever of you is present in the month, let him fast it. So the fast follows the book. Muslims understand that the Qur'an's revelation began in Ramadan, on a night called Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, which this path reaches soon. And there's a scene in Bukhari that makes the month feel like a study partnership. Ibn 'Abbas says the Prophet ﷺ was the most generous of people, and most generous of all in Ramadan, when Jibril met him every night of the month and went over the Qur'an with him. When Jibril met him, Ibn 'Abbas says, he was more generous with good than the wind sent forth. Another report says Jibril reviewed the whole Qur'an with him once each Ramadan, and twice in the last year of his life. So for many Muslims, Ramadan isn't only about what you don't eat. It's about what you take in. Mosques fill at night for the long tarawih prayers, where the Qur'an is recited in sections. Some who rarely open the book during the year try to read it all. Whatever else the month is, its first verse names it by a book.
screen: `THE MONTH IN WHICH THE QUR'AN CAME.` · `THE FAST FOLLOWS THE BOOK.` · `JIBRIL, EVERY NIGHT OF RAMADAN.` · `MORE GENEROUS THAN THE WIND.`

segments.voice: If you have a Qur'an or an app nearby, read or listen to a few verses, slowly, in Arabic or in translation. If you don't, sit with the verse you just heard: the month in which the Qur'an was revealed. Let that be enough for today.
Ramadan. The ninth month, the month of fasting, introduced in the Qur'an first as the month in which the Qur'an was revealed. Today's word.
Your line: the month of the book. Hunger is only half the story. Day five hundred eight, done.

howItsDone: During Ramadan, many Muslims give extra time to the Qur'an, reading it alone or hearing it in the nightly tarawih prayers, where long portions are recited aloud; the month is also a time of increased charity.

chat.says: Is Ramadan just about not eating?
options: It's first named as the month the Qur'an was revealed; the fast follows.
Yes, the Qur'an names the month only for the fast from dawn to sunset.

chat.meaning: Verse 2:185 names the month by its book first: the month in which was revealed the Qur'an. Only then does it say to fast.
